title: Allow to temporarily disable notifications/enter DND mode for individual apps
line: Each notification has a Do not disturb button that silences just its app for 1 hour, 4 hours, until this evening or tomorrow morning.
explanation: Do not disturb mode only existed for the whole system; the only per-app option was turning off an app's popups permanently in System Settings, with no timer and several clicks away. Popups, history notifications and history app groups now have a Do not disturb button (bell with slash) next to Configure. It opens the same duration menu as the global switch (without "Until manually disabled"); while the app is muted its notifications skip the popup and land in the history, the button shows as checked with the end time in its tooltip, and clicking it again or reaching the end time unmutes the app. Notifications held back during the mute are marked as expired at unmute so they don't all pop up at once.

commits.message:
applets/notifications: allow do not disturb mode for a single app

Do not disturb mode could only silence every app at once. Notifications
now have a button that mutes their app for a while, so its notifications
go straight to the history without popping up until the time runs out.

BUG: 452500

media.caption: Before: a popup only offers Close (and Configure for known apps)
After: the new Do not disturb button on the popup opens the duration menu
Before: history app groups have no way to silence the app
After: Thunderbird muted for 1 hour: its new notifications only went to the history, the group's button is checked and its tooltip shows when it ends
Muting Thunderbird from its popup: the popup goes away, the next Thunderbird notification doesn't pop up, a Konsole one still does
After unmuting, the notifications held back during the mute stay in the history and don't pop up
